Q1: Hexanoic acid shows a Known Hazard (Tier 1) for dermal and eye hazards (SKN1) based on official GHS classifications. It also has Expanded Perspective (Tier 2) hazards for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, and reproductive hazards (CMR2), environmental hazards (ENV2), and inhalation hazards (IHL2). Oral hazards (ORL3) and endocrine disruption hazards (EDC3) are considered low to moderate concern, while organ and systemic hazards (OGN4) are data deficient, indicating an area where more information is needed.
Q2: This chemical is not present on any identified lists of concern. However, it is recognized on two lists of low hazard: the SCIL Green Circle list, indicating it has been verified as low concern, and the EPA's Substances Added to Food inventory, suggesting its use as an ingredient regulated by the FDA.
Q3: Hexanoic acid is extensively characterized, with 38,000 literature references, significantly higher than the median for chemicals in our dataset. Its molecular formula (C6H12O2) is precisely defined, and it is classified as a 'Small Molecule,' further indicating a well-understood structure. Only one hazard class (OGN4) remains data deficient in its tier profile, suggesting a relatively complete hazard assessment.
